species.name: Shortnose Sturgeon
species.quote: It is illegal to take, possess, land, purchase, or sell any of the following species: Atlantic sturgeon Diamondback terrapin Shortnose sturgeon River herring (alewife and blueback herring; see herring illustrations) Various shark species (See Sharks)
species.notes: Also listed as a protected species in the Freshwater Digest ("It is illegal to take, possess, land, purchase, or sell any of these species.").
userNotes: Protected in all NJ waters, salt and fresh. Release immediately if caught.

species.name: Horseshoe Crab
species.quote: The harvest of horseshoe crabs is prohibited. Possession of horseshoe crabs is also prohibited except for those individuals holding a scientific collecting permit for research and education and those fishermen that can provide suitable documentation that the horseshoe crabs in their possession were harvested outside of New Jersey.
species.notes: Exception only for scientific collecting permit holders or documented out-of-state harvest.
userNotes: No recreational harvest or possession of horseshoe crabs in New Jersey.

species.name: Atlantic Herring
species.quote: Dip nets 24 inches diameter or less for taking Atlantic herring only for live bait. The taking or possession of river herring (alewife and blueback herring) is prohibited.
species.notes: Bait fish gear rule: may be taken for personal use as live bait with dip nets 24 inches diameter or less without a license. Fish taken this way may not be sold or bartered without a commercial bait net license.

zones.label: NJ marine waters
zones.bagNote: No limit printed; personal-use bait only

userNotes: Dip net must be 24 inches in diameter or less and may only be used for Atlantic herring for live bait.
Do not confuse with river herring (alewife, blueback) — those are prohibited.

species.name: Shellfish (recreational aggregate)
species.quote: No holder of any recreational shellfish license may take more than a total of 150 shellfish (in aggregate) per day. See Shellfish License Information. ... Shellfish means any species of benthic mollusks (except conch) including hard and soft clams, oysters, surf clams, bay scallops and mussels.
species.season: Open year-round; harvest prohibited before sunrise/after sunset and on Sundays (except Navesink & Shrewsbury seasonally approved areas Nov 1–Apr 30)
species.size: None printed except hard clam 1 1/2 inches
species.notes: Recreational shellfish license required. Hand implements only on public grounds; dredging prohibited. Harvest from condemned or leased waters prohibited. Non-resident recreational license valid June–September only.

zones.label: NJ shellfish growing waters (approved/seasonally approved areas)
zones.sizeNote: No minimum printed for species other than hard clam (1 1/2 inches)

userNotes: The 150-per-day limit is a combined total across all shellfish species (clams, oysters, surf clams, bay scallops, mussels).
No shellfishing before sunrise, after sunset, or on Sundays (except Navesink/Shrewsbury seasonally approved areas Nov 1–Apr 30).
Check the Shellfish Growing Water Classification Charts before harvesting — condemned waters are closed even for bait.

species.name: Eastern Oyster
species.quote: Specific seasons, regulations and size limits exist for oyster beds in Great Bay, Delaware Bay, plus the Mullica, Great Egg Harbor and Tuckahoe rivers. Check with the nearest shellfish office (Nacote Creek or Delaware Bay) for these detailed regulations. Shells taken in the process of harvesting oysters must be culled from the live oysters and returned immediately to the area from where they were taken.
species.season: See shellfish office for bed-specific seasons
species.size: See shellfish office for bed-specific size limits
species.limit: Counts toward 150 shellfish aggregate per day
species.notes: Shellfish license required. Shells must be culled and returned to the harvest area.

zones.label: NJ oyster beds (Great Bay, Delaware Bay, Mullica, Great Egg Harbor, Tuckahoe rivers)
zones.bagNote: Part of the 150-shellfish aggregate per day; bed-specific rules apply
zones.sizeNote: Bed-specific size limits — call Nacote Creek (609) 748-2020 or Delaware Bay shellfish office

userNotes: Oysters count toward your 150-shellfish daily aggregate.
Oyster beds have their own seasons and size limits not printed in the digest — call the Nacote Creek or Delaware Bay shellfish office before harvesting.

species.quote: Sharks | Aggregated large coastal group, Hammerhead group: Jan 1–May 14 and July 16–Dec 31 | Non-blacknose small coastal group: No Closed Season | Blacknose group: No Closed Season | Pelagic group: No Closed Season | Minimum Length (fork length): Atlantic sharpnose, bonnethead, and smoothhound: None; Hammerheads 78"; All other retainable sharks: 54" | Prohibited sharks: Zero allowed possession; Shortfin mako: Zero allowed possession; Smoothhound: No limit; All others: One per person per trip | Use of non-offset, corrodible, non-stainless steel circle hooks is required, except when fishing with flies or artificial lures. ... Shark Species That May Be Kept (Authorized Species): Aggregated Large Coastal Shark—blacktip, bull, lemon, nurse, tiger, spinner; Hammerhead Shark—scalloped hammerhead, smooth hammerhead, great hammerhead; Non-Blacknose Small Coastal Shark—Atlantic sharpnose, bonnethead, finetooth; Blacknose Shark—blacknose; Pelagic Shark—blue, porbeagle, and common thresher.
species.notes: Group members: blacktip, bull, lemon, nurse, tiger, spinner. Closed May 15–July 15 in state waters to protect pupping females.
userNotes: Closed in NJ state waters May 15 through July 15.
Non-offset, corrodible, non-stainless steel circle hooks required when fishing for sharks with anything other than flies or artificial lures.
Sharks must be landed with head, tail and fins naturally attached; filleting at sea is prohibited (gutting and bleeding allowed).
Length is fork length, not total length.
Federal waters (3–200 nm) follow NOAA HMS rules and require an HMS permit — see fisheries.noaa.gov.

userNotes: Shortfin mako must be released; zero possession in NJ.

species.name: Sharks — Prohibited species
species.quote: Shark Species That MUST Be Released (Prohibited Species): Atlantic angel, basking, bigeye sand tiger, bigeye sixgill, bigeye thresher, bignose, Caribbean reef, Caribbean sharpnose, dusky, Galapagos, longfin mako, narrowtooth, night, oceanic whitetip, sandbar, sand tiger, sevengill, silky, sixgill, smalltail, whale and white. ... Prohibited sharks: Zero allowed possession
species.notes: Federal rules prohibit targeting; release immediately without removing from the water.
userNotes: Release immediately in the water — do not bring ashore or pose for photos (federal violation).
Sandbar and sand tiger are common NJ catches and are on this list.

species.name: Striped Bass (fresh waters)
species.quote: STRIPED BASS (FRESHWATER ONLY) | Striped Bass | March 1–Dec. 31 Please check website for possible Striped Bass regulation changes during 2026. | Statewide Non-offset circle hook required when fishing with bait | One @ 28" to a maximum of 31" | 1
species.size: 28 inch to a maximum of 31 inch slot
species.notes: Freshwater digest rule for non-tidal waters; marine rows cover tidal/marine waters. Non-offset circle hook required with bait.

zones.label: Delaware River upstream of Calhoun St. Bridge
Delaware River downstream of Calhoun St. Bridge

userNotes: Delaware River quote: 'Striped Bass & Hybrids** (upstream of Calhoun St. Bridge) | March 1–Dec. 31 | One @ 28" to a maximum of 31" | 1' and '(downstream of Calhoun St. Bridge) | March 1–31 ... June 1–Dec. 31'.
Pennsylvania's Apr 1–May 31 Delaware River slot season does not apply if you land in NJ — NJ is closed Apr 1–May 31 below Calhoun St. Bridge.
Non-offset (inline) circle hooks required when fishing with bait.

issues: curl to dep.nj.gov and eregulations.com is blocked by the agent proxy (CONNECT 403), so the 2026 Marine Digest PDF, Freshwater Digest PDF, 'Attention Anglers' sheet and Recreational Seasons Summary Chart could not be downloaded or text-extracted. The DEP seasons-and-regulations and freshwater pages only link to those PDFs (no HTML table). All values were therefore read from the publisher's HTML edition of the same 2026 digests on eregulations.com (linked from https://dep.nj.gov/njfw/digests/marine/ as 'Publisher's Online 2026 New Jersey Marine Digest'), which the brief allows as an official source.

Shark minimum size conflict within the digest: the table says 'All other retainable sharks: 54"' but the text says 'In state waters, there is no minimum size limit for non-blacknose small coastal sharks and blacknose sharks' (federal 54" for blacknose and finetooth). Modeled both in sizeNote; recommend treating 54" FL as the safe rule.

Hickory shad: Delaware River freshwater page prints 'Shad, Hickory | Closed' while the marine table allows 6 shad (max 2 American) in 'Delaware River & tributaries'. Likely tidal vs non-tidal split (fishing license boundary lines) but the digest does not say so explicitly.
American shad: freshwater table says 'Delaware River Mainstem' only; marine table says 'Delaware River & tributaries'. Flagged in corrections.
Snapping turtle, bull/green frog, diamondback terrapin are printed with seasons/limits/prohibitions but are not fish or shellfish; not added (schema habitat enum). Listed in speciesOnSourceNotAdded.

Freshwater 'Trout' nuance (TCAs, Catch and Release Areas, Wild Trout Streams, trophy/holdover lakes, Delaware River) was captured as zones on the new Brook/Brown/Rainbow rows and as corrections on the existing Trout row rather than rewriting that row.
Striped Bass Bonus Program modeled as a correction (add 'bonus' zone) rather than a new species to avoid a duplicate Striped Bass row.
